reader_notes.title: Exit-map classification barrier - every efficiently computable algebraic homomorphism out of a prime-order prime-field subgroup lands in one of three classes, each with an exponent at or above one half, and self-maps are provably exponent-neutral
reader_notes.test: Four stages, all executable at toy scale, none requiring a solver breakthrough. (1) INDEX THEOREM CHECK. On toy curves at 12, 16, 20 and 24 bits with prime-order G, and for r in {1, 2, 3, 4} using phi_1 = identity, phi_2 = negation-independent CM endomorphism where available, phi_3 = phi_2^2, and phi_4 = Frobenius-derived scalar, construct W_r explicitly from the publicly computable eigenvalues lambda_i and report its Hermite normal form index, its determinant, and lambda_1^infty via exact enumeration or LLL with a certified bound. Predicted index N for all r. (2) MITM COST CURVE. For each r, run the balanced meet-in-the-middle over the 2r coordinates in the Minkowski box, counting group operations and memory, and report cost / sqrt(N) as a function of r. Compare against matched Pollard rho with negation at 0.886 sqrt(N) and matched BSGS. (3) SHORT-WITNESS DISTRIBUTION. At toy N (12-20 bits) enumerate ALL scalars k, compute lambda_1^infty(L_k) exactly by enumeration, and compare the empirical CDF against both the rigorous bound 4 eps^2 and the Siegel mean-value prediction for random lattices of covolume N. Report the tail: the single smallest lambda_1^infty observed and its predicted frequency. (4) COVER-EXIT COST. Build explicit covers C: y^2 = f(varphi(t)) for varphi of degree d in {1, 2, 3}, giving genus g about 3d/2; verify pi^* is injective on G by checking gcd(N, d) = 1 and by replaying pi^*(P) and pi^*(Q) as reduced divisors; then run a standard Jacobian index calculus (degree-one factor base, sparse solve) on the transported instance and fit the cost exponent in log_p units across at least three field sizes. Report every stage in group-operation equivalents against matched rho.

predictions.minimum_effect: [Z^{2r} : W_r] = N exactly, for every tested r in {1, 2, 3, 4} and every tested instance, computed as the Smith normal form / Hermite normal form index of the explicitly constructed lattice. Any instance with index strictly less than N falsifies C1 and is a scoped positive requiring independent review.

Measured meet-in-the-middle cost of finding a witness in W_r, divided by sqrt(N), is non-decreasing in r and grows at least like 2^{r-1} between r = 1 and r = 4, with the r = 1 value within a factor 2 of 1. A ratio that DECREASES with r at any tested size falsifies the neutrality claim and is the single most informative possible outcome of this record.

Over exhaustive enumeration of all k in [1, N-1] at toy N, the fraction of scalars with lambda_1^infty(L_k) <= eps sqrt(N) is at most 4 eps^2 + 3/sqrt(N) for every eps in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4}, and the empirical mean of lambda_1^infty / sqrt(N) agrees with the Siegel mean-value prediction within 5 percent. A systematic excess of short witnesses is a structural signal.

For explicit covers C = E x_{P^1} P^1_varphi of genus g in {2, 3, 4, 5} over the SAME toy prime field, the fitted cost exponent of the best available Jacobian index calculus, expressed in log_p units, is at least 1.0 - 0.15 at every tested size, versus 0.5 for matched rho on the original curve. A fitted exponent below 0.5 falsifies C3.

For every curve in the public census, the computed triple (N == p, ord_N(p), minimal cover exponent over tested g) assigns the curve to exactly one of E1, E2, E3 or to "no exit", with zero curves unassigned. Any curve carrying an efficiently computable homomorphism out of G that the triple fails to classify falsifies C2.

reader_notes.title: Endomorphism-rank cost curve - the cheapest decisive test that adding endomorphisms to the ECDLP witness lattice shrinks the Minkowski minimum while leaving the search exponent at one half and inflating the constant
reader_notes.test: Toy prime-field curves at 16, 20, 24, 28 and 32 bits, prime-order subgroups, at least 5 seeds each, on three families: j = 0 (|Aut| = 6), j = 1728 (|Aut| = 4), and generic j (|Aut| = 2, the control family). For each instance and each r in {1, 2, 3, 4}: (1) compute the eigenvalues lambda_i from the characteristic equation modulo N and verify each by checking phi_i(P) = [lambda_i]P on the curve - a check that costs O(log N) and catches a wrong root immediately; (2) construct W_r explicitly as the kernel lattice of the single congruence, compute its Hermite normal form, report the index and the determinant; (3) compute lambda_1^infty(W_r) exactly by enumeration for dimension <= 4 and by LLL with a certified gap for dimension 6 and 8, reporting which method was used per instance; (4) run the balanced meet-in-the-middle over the 2r coordinates in the Minkowski box, counting group operations and peak memory, and verify the returned witness by replaying sum_i a_i phi_i(P) + sum_i b_i phi_i(Q) = O on the curve and by recovering k = -A/B mod N and checking [k]P = Q. Only certificate-verified witnesses are counted; (5) run matched Pollard rho with negation and the automorphism quotient where available, and matched BSGS, on the same instances; (6) plot cost/sqrt(N) and memory against r, and the fitted shrinkage slope against 1/(2r), on the same axes.

predictions.minimum_effect: Hermite normal form index equals N exactly on 100 percent of instances for every r in {1, 2, 3, 4}. Any single instance with index below N falsifies P1.

The fitted slope of log_N(lambda_1^infty(W_r)) against 1/(2r) lies in [0.85, 1.15] with R^2 >= 0.90, confirming genuine shrinkage. A flat curve would mean the Minkowski bound is not attained and the setup is wrong, making the cost comparison uninterpretable.

The measured ratio is non-decreasing in r and at least 4x larger at r = 4 than at r = 1, with the r = 1 value within a factor 2 of 1. The competing prediction - a ratio DECREASING in r at any tested size - is the single most informative possible outcome and would require independent review before interpretation.

Measured rho cost on j = 0 and j = 1728 curves lies within 20 percent of 0.886 sqrt(N / |Aut|), i.e. the endomorphism benefit is exactly the classical automorphism quotient and nothing more. A measured speedup exceeding sqrt(|Aut|) by more than 20 percent is a signal that must be explained before any other number in the run is trusted.

Peak memory of the augmented MITM divided by rho's peak memory is at least sqrt(N)/polylog at every r, confirming Pareto domination by rho. A memory-competitive MITM would change the tradeoff reading.

reader_notes.title: Public-scalar factor base — the linear-algebra and relation-collection stages of prime-field index calculus are removable by construction, and the standing alpha < 3/2 gate belongs to a dominated variant
reader_notes.test: (1) INSTANCES: toy prime-field curves at 16, 20, 24 bits, prime-order subgroups, 3 seeds; m in {3, 4, 5}; B = ceil((m!*N)^(1/m)) (tight beta = 1/m). (2) DIRECT VARIANT: build F = {s_i*P} with fresh public random scalars (distinct +/- classes); for each of >= 10 targets, run t-randomized attempts (fresh t per attempt) with the committed Semaev membership test until one success; read off k = +/-sum(s) - t; verify by re-multiplication (certificate). Record total group ops per target including ALL failed attempts. (3) UNKNOWN-LOG VARIANT (control): same base but scalars hidden; run relation collection to rank B-1, the sparse solve, then the same descent; record S_rel, S_LA, T_desc. (4) ALPHA MEASUREMENT: independently fit the amortized query exponent per IDEA-20260727-007 from a separate campaign. (5) COVERAGE: exact enumeration of reachable targets at the smallest size; the conservation identity check (mean = binomial(B+m-1,m)/N). (6) Fit E_direct_measured, report intervals, and assemble the comparison table vs 0.5 and vs matched rho.

predictions.minimum_effect: Fitted E_direct_measured (total group ops per target, yield-charged, vs N on log-log axes, R^2 >= 0.90 over >= 3 sizes) equals alpha/m within 0.05 at m in {3, 4, 5} and is < 1/2 at >= 1 tested (m, size) cell. The falsifier: E_direct_measured >= 1/2 at ALL tested cells.

On identical instances, (S_rel + S_LA + K*T_desc) for the unknown-log variant (scalars hidden, matrix solve) is >= the direct variant's total for K >= 1 at every tested cell; a measured ratio < 1 would mean the unknown-log variant has an unmodeled advantage and the budget correction is incomplete.

The alpha implied by E_direct_measured (alpha = m * E_direct_measured) agrees with the independently measured amortized query exponent (per IDEA-20260727-007's pre-registration: total query cost over a campaign / usable relations) within 0.1 at every cell — the self-consistency check that the exponent is being attributed to the right stage.

Measured attempts-per-success lies in [1, 2] * m! / coverage at every cell with coverage measured by exact enumeration at the smallest size — the EV-FBG-001 conservation-identity check, confirming no uncharged yield factor.

reason: Public-scalar bases test the mandatory-linear-algebra premise directly; endomorphism rank and exit-map proposals share related older controls whose full source coverage must be checked. Audit overlap and live ownership before additive designs; no barrier, exhaustive classification or exponent claim accepted from source prose.
